generation_prompt:
Edit the supplied image as the DIRECT art base for Figure 1 of the STaR-Body CVPR paper. This is the user's preferred original Gemini figure; preserve its dense, detailed scientific-illustration style extremely closely. Do NOT simplify, replace its typography with oversized labels, flatten it into a sparse block diagram, or redraw it as generic vector boxes. Retain the small realistic video frames, token-grid projection illustration, articulated skeletons, six anatomical part icons, learned-query token illustrations, kinematic tree, and gray 3-D output mesh. Retain the exact muted gray / slate blue / teal / parchment yellow / dusty mauve palette, nested panels and elegant compact captions. Produce a clean high-resolution wide figure, about 2.45:1 aspect ratio, with very thin white margins. All labels in English. Rich technical detail like the source; crisp typography and formulas.

Preserve the five original regions and their titles:
left gray "Offline Monocular Person Track" with 17-frame source and "8 target frames 4–11"; frozen HMR 2.0a image tokens, frozen VACE context and frozen initial SMPL reference;
blue "Stage 1: Dual-Order Spatiotemporal Decoder";
top center teal "Track-Shape Conditioning";
center ochre "Stage 2: Joint-Indexed Landmark Feedback";
right mauve "Stage 3: Part-Aware Iterative Rotation Refiner".

Only correct/clarify technical content needed for the real implementation, while retaining the original visual richness:
1. HMR 2.0a has a 16 × 12 grid: "192 image tokens / frame", "width 1280", sampled around projected joints. VACE input is 17 frames, five latent grids, each pooled to 2 × 3, making 30 memory tokens. Label latent width 1536 separately if used; it is not the projected decoder width. Frozen initial reference supplies pose R₀, shape β₀ and camera c₀.
2. Stage 1: 26 body queries = 24 pose + shape + camera, width 256. Preserve the two mathematical attention paths "Space → Time", Z_ST=A_T(A_S(Z)), and "Time → Space", Z_TS=A_S(A_T(Z)), their weighted mixture Z′=a₁Z_ST+a₂Z_TS, and base body state R, β, c. Label "3 shared decoder iterations". These are distinct from the three final rotation-refinement iterations.
3. Track-shape: replace "median shape" with "Robust weighted shape β̄" and retain "RGB feature f̄". The prototype is computed offline from fixed-decoder predictions; the median determines robust weights, it is not the prototype itself. Shared correction Δβ_track=0.3 tanh(MLP([f̄;β̄])). Explicitly route this correction to the shape state/bypass, not into landmark tokens.
4. Stage 2: maintain the illustrated seven-dimensional landmark feature stack and exactly "17 landmark evidence tokens": residual e=sg(û)−p (2), current projection p (2), log-variance (1), visibility (1), validity (1). The inherited predicted-landmark features are stop-gradient conditioning. Token encoder "7 → 128 → 128" plus Landmark ID and Schema ID ("COCO / PoseTrack"). The current body's projection and the inherited predicted observations are inputs to this evidence block. Show 24 learned pose queries, 17 landmark K/V tokens and a 24-joint SMPL tree. Preserve the compact "Anatomical Cross-Attention (4 heads)" inset; its soft bias is −0.5 × D(j,a(l)) plus a valid-landmark mask. Total width 128, four heads of 32 channels. Correct the zero-initialized final output projection label to "Wₒ = 0 at initialization", not approximately zero. It produces 24 × 128 joint-feedback tokens.
5. Correct the connection into Stage 3: joint-feedback tokens must be ADDED to existing per-joint features BEFORE anatomical part pooling. Insert a compact small "Local image + body/query features" card feeding an ADD junction together with the joint-feedback tokens; the junction then feeds anatomical part pooling. Do NOT imply that feedback alone is the complete joint representation. Keep the six anatomical icons: Root, Torso/head, L arm, R arm, L leg, R leg. Then "Part/Time Block — residual spatiotemporal attention", followed by "Grouped GRU & Iterative Refiner — width 128", "3 refinement iterations". The GRU recurs across refinement steps.
6. Change local sampling-radius units from px to "2 → 1 → 0.5 token cells". Preserve the bounded axis-angle formula ωʳ = α tanh(u)/sqrt(1+||tanh(u)||²) and Rʳ⁺¹=exp([ωʳ]×)Rʳ, with "2° root / 5° joint per step" and "6° / 15° cumulative bounds". Shape β and camera c remain fixed throughout this final rotation stage.
7. The shape/camera bypass must originate from the Stage 1 body state, with the track-shape correction applied to β, and join the updated rotations at the final SMPL mesh. It MUST NOT branch from the joint-feedback tokens. Use clean routed lines at the panel edges.
8. The final refinement feedback loop starts at updated rotations, recomputes current SMPL projection and local image sampling, and returns to Stage 2 evidence and Stage 3 local features. It must not imply that the full Stage 1 decoder is repeatedly rerun by the final refiner. Keep the blue-stage internal three-iteration indication separate.
9. Remove the entire bottom prompt-like footer beginning "NO performance metrics..." and the redundant vertical "Input & Frozen Encoders Column" instruction strip. Keep only a clean functional bottom return-loop label "Current SMPL projection & local image resampling".
Preserve the original level of detail and close module spacing; improve arrow alignment and label fit only. No statistical scores, new losses, unrelated modules, bright saturated colors, bevelled plastic UI, decorative giant headings, or simplification. Output the publication figure only, without a caption outside it.
One further exact source-arrow correction: inside Stage 2 the vertical arrow between the 17-token feature block and the attention block points DOWNWARD: encoded evidence supplies K/V to attention. Do not keep the original mistaken upward arrow from attention into evidence.

All arrows thin charcoal, orthogonal with unmistakable arrowheads and no text crossing. Keep original appearance, module count, crowded scientific richness, and all content not mentioned above. Do not insert new content. Output the corrected figure.
